neighboring_unit_entries.title: Small radial derivative distance is not exclusively a close-gap phenomenon
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source explicitly blocks a tempting converse by citing separated-root families that still produce near-circle derivative roots, then explains why close pairs nevertheless determine the leading square-root density and records the unresolved normalization problem.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: A close root pair creates a unique nearby derivative root whose even analytic displacement starts quadratically in the gap, so pushing the repulsive small-gap spacing density through this map produces a square-root near-boundary density.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This accounts for the leading close-pair contribution only and relies on ensemble information for background-root coefficients.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The multiple-root limit supplies a base point for an analytic perturbation: an even, gap-controlled root displacement can then push eigenvalue repulsion into a fractional-power density.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Starting from a coincident eigenvalue pair, the nearby Λ′ root moves continuously as the centered rescaled pair separates by θ; with δ=N(1−z′), the source states an even expansion δ=b₁π²θ²+b₂π⁴θ⁴+O(θ⁶) and derives the close-pair contribution 4s^(1/2)/(3π)−82s^(3/2)/(45π)+O(s^(5/2)) as N grows.
directed.conceptual_reading: Degeneracy is used constructively as a solvable anchor, and the quadratic local map explains why cubic small-gap repulsion becomes a square-root output density.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is a pushforward from centered nearest-neighbor gap θ to scaled derivative-root displacement δ via an analytic local branch.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Theorem 3.1 describes small δ arising from close pairs, not the complete small-δ population.
directed.uncertainty: Moderate: the perturbative construction is explicit, but exact coefficients in the two expansions are formula-layer dependent.

supported: The span anchors the nearby derivative root at a double-root limit, centers the pair, states an even θ expansion for the complex displacement, and gives the close-pair density asymptotic.
The candidate correctly limits Theorem 3.1 to small distances arising from close pairs.
inference: The quadratic-map explanation for converting cubic gap repulsion to a square-root density is a grounded pushforward interpretation.
unsupported_or_imported: The directed account attaches the density conclusion to δ=N(1−z′) without distinguishing that complex displacement from the radial observable N(1−|z′|) used in the theorem statement.
context_or_ocr_risk: The extracted theorem reuses δ inconsistently, so the candidate must disambiguate rather than inherit the notation collision.
missed_mechanism: Projection from complex root displacement to radial distance is required before stating the probability-density pushforward.
revision_instructions: Separate the analytic expansion for complex δ_c=N(1−z′) from the density for radial δ_r=N(1−|z′|); state that later radialization and spacing pushforward produce the displayed close-pair law.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Ratio averages reduce random root coefficients to computable expectations
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A generating ratio of characteristic polynomials converts the needed collision-conditioned coefficient moments into derivatives of a known Haar average; computer algebra then supplies the expected second coefficient and closes Theorem 3.1.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Observed zeta-prime radial analogue matches the CUE distribution shape
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Approximately one hundred thousand derivative zeros in a stated height interval give an empirical distribution with the same striking overall shape as derivative roots of unitary characteristic polynomials.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Matching local mean spacing converts horizontal displacement from the critical line and radial displacement from the unit circle into parallel scaled variables, after which the close-pair logarithmic-derivative equations have the same leading form.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The zeta side depends on CUE statistics and asymptotic approximations; agreement is solver-independent mathematical evidence only for the model correspondence, not for RH.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Mean-spacing normalization transports a derivative-zero law between two geometries

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Speiser supplies an exact exclusion criterion, while Levinson-style losses and Soundararajan frequency functions turn finer right-of-line proximity into quantitative diagnostics that the CUE calculation can model.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The frequency conjectures and zeta/CUE match remain conditional or conjectural, and none of the source's distributional calculations proves the exclusion required by RH.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Derivative-zero proximity is a graded diagnostic rather than a direct RH proof route

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: After peeling two close poles from ζ′/ζ and measuring everything in local mean-spacing units, the residual zero field enters the same implicit equation as the background roots of a CUE polynomial.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The partial-fraction expansion of ζ′/ζ separates two close zeros around height t from all other zeros. With X=x/log t and gap Θ=2πθ/log t, expansion gives the same leading implicit form as in the unitary calculation, including β₁≈1/4; assuming CUE zero statistics supplies the expected background coefficient and hence the matching leading ζ′ law.
directed.conceptual_reading: Mean-spacing normalization reveals that the shared object is a local logarithmic-derivative balance, not merely a visual resemblance between two distributions.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Zeta zeros become rescaled poles in a partial-fraction field, parallel to reciprocal distances from CUE roots; the background coefficient is then evaluated through the collision-weighted one-level density.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The expected coefficient and final distributional match assume CUE statistics and asymptotic approximations, so the zeta conclusion is conjectural and does not prove RH.
directed.uncertainty: Moderate to high for exact algebra because equations (6.1)–(6.17) are dense and fragmented; the conditional structural match is explicit in prose.

supported: The span separates a chosen close ζ-zero pair in ζ′/ζ, rescales gap and displacement by log t, derives the same leading implicit form and coefficients as the CUE calculation, and makes the final law conditional on CUE spacing statistics.

inference: Identifying the shared mechanism as a local logarithmic-derivative balance is a substantive and grounded bridge.
